INSTRUCTIONS FOR THE DECEMBER 2, 2020
  OLD TOWN LA VERNE BUSINESS IMPROVEMENT DISTRICT SPECIAL MEETING

The Old Town La Verne Business Improvement District meeting will be closed to the public in
compliance with Governor Newsom’s Executive Order to minimize the spread of the COVID-
19 Virus. Additionally, the meeting will be conducted via teleconference with members
participating remotely. Considering this, the customary meeting format has been modified.
Even with this change in format, the City is still encouraging public participation and wishes to
make residents aware of the following opportunities for participation:

  1) View the meeting through the City’s website at www.cityoflaverne.org/stream

  2) Please submit your written comments via email at planning@cityoflaverne.org. They
  will be shared with the District Board Members prior to the meeting and will be made
  part of the permanent record. We ask that you provide those emails before 7:00 p.m.
  the day before the meeting.

  3) For individuals that wish to share their comments during the live stream, you may
  email planning@cityoflaverne.org by 7:00 a.m. on the day of the meeting with a phone
  number and the item(s) you wish to speak on. We will call you back at the appropriate
  time during the meeting for your comment.

OLD TOWN LA VERNE BUSINESS IMPROYEMENT DISTIRICT
  MINUTES OF THE SPECIAL MEETING
  Wednesday, December 2,, 2020

I  The teleconference meeting was called to order by Chairperson Craig Walters at 8:30a.m
  Chairperson Walters stated that questions can be emailed to planning@citloflaverne.org.

  Advisory Board Members present: Craig Walters, Chris Cendreau, Jason Miller.
  Marianne Stark, Micky Rehm and Matt Forgey. City Representatives present:
  Community Development Director Eric Scherer, Administrative Clerk Natalie Hiatt, and
  Mayor Tim Hepburn. Others present: Leah Skinner.

  Chairperson walters remembered Brian McNerney of the La Verne chamber of
  commerce. Mr. McNerney unexpectedly passed the morning of rhanksgiving.

)  CALENDAR

  Cool Cruise - Rescheduled - Date to be determined.

3.  APPROVAL OF MINUTES None

4.  NEW BUSINESS None

5.  CONTINUED BUSINESS

  A.  D Street Closure - Chairperson Walters recapped that last week Los Angeles
  County ordered that all outdoor dining stop and be limited to takeout and delivery
  for three weeks. He stated concem for the businesses on D Street that were utilizing
  the street closure and invested in outdoor dining setups. The City polled members
  and it was decided to keep the barriers in place until more information was provided
  regarding the court case filed by the califomia Restaurant Association.

  Mr. Scherer stated that since the order was issued there has been discussion of a new
  Safer at Home order issued by the State that would presumptively extend outdoor dining
  closure further. He stated that it was temporarily decided to leave the street closed. The
  City is now looking for direction from the Board. There were four Public Comments
  received.

  Ms. Stark asked if it would be considered outdoor dining if the restaurants left their
  outdoor dining area in place for takeout diners.

  Mr. Scherer stated that it would be considered outdoor dining because it's an extension of
  their restaurant area as permitted by the City, Alcohol Beverage Control, and Los
  Angeles County Health Department.

  I
 Ms. Stark asked if City owned park benches can be added to the center of D Street for
takeout.

Mr. Scherer stated that it has been discussed but there is some risk in facilitating. The
City needs to investigate with their insurance company.

Chairperson Walters stated that there were mixed feelings about opening the street last
week but those that he spoke to directly supported opening the street if there was no
activity in the street.

Mr. Gendreau suggested waiting for the outcome of the court case before making a
decision. He stated that many restaurants in Glendora and Claremont are going against
the order and have remained open.

Ms. Rehm stated that Downtown is dead and only one restaurant is still utilizing the
space. She stated that by re-opening the street there would be more activity and easier
access for the consumers.

Ms. Stark asked if City Council can override the order.

Mr. Scherer stated that the City is taking hands off approach. If complaints are received
the Police Department will follow-up and educate the businesses.

Mayor Hepburn stated that as of yesterday there are 832 COVID cases and I 5 deaths. He
stated that he is not agreement of the order but we must abide by it.

Chairperson Walters stated that this special meeting was called in hopes that the court's
decision would be made but it was delayed.

Mr. Forgey stated support in the street remaining closed if the coun case is successful.

Ms. Rehm stated that she hopes the court case is in favor of the restaurants but if it does
not rule in favor, the street should be re-opened.

Mr. Miller recommended that the Board agree upon a timeframe to re-open the street
based upon the court's decision.

Mr. Scherer stated the decision can be handled at a staff level but City Council will be
informed and given the opportunity to add the item to the City Council agenda for
Monday's meeting.

Ms. Stark recommended waiting until the Monday BID meeting for a decision.

It was moved by Mr. Gendreau and seconded by Ms. Stark to recommend the City
continue the street closure for outdoor dining if a positive court decision is received.
However, if the decision is not in favor of the restaurants the City should start the process

  2
   of re-opening the street. If the court case is not decided today the DBID will wait untilthe
  regularly scheduled meeting Monday to decide. Motion carried by a 5-0 vote.

  Mr. Gendreau asked if the Business Assistance Grant was still available and if those that
  already received money can re-apply for more assistance.

  Mr. Scherer stated there are still funds available and it's a possibility that the Committee
  will decide to allow businesses to apply for more assistance. He encouraged those that
  have not applied to submit their applications.

  Mayor Hepburn stated that the businesses have the Council's full support.
